subject: 20260913-164409-sweep-deepgram-30
headline: While the voice agent achieves a 100.0% task success rate, tail latency degrades to 2543.9 ms at just 5 concurrent calls, driven by thinking time bottlenecks.

insights.title: Tail Latency Spikes Under Minimal Load
insights.finding: While the baseline step has a p95 response wait of 1149.5 ms, introducing even a light load of 5 concurrent calls causes the p95 response wait to rise to 2543.9 ms, and further to 3108.9 ms at 10 concurrent calls.
insights.why_it_matters: At concurrent call counts of 5 and higher, the system violates the Coval target of 2000 ms, meaning the slowest 5% of callers will experience jarring delays of over two seconds.
insights.next_step: Optimize resource allocation for the agent at concurrency levels above baseline to ensure consistent response times.

insights.title: Final Turn Bottleneck
insights.finding: On the final turn of the conversation (turn 5), the p95 response wait climbs to 3236.8 ms, whereas earlier turns like turn 1 and turn 4 remain at 1100.9 ms and 1210.1 ms respectively.
insights.why_it_matters: The slowest callers face a long pause of 3236.8 ms on the final turn when the agent is only saying goodbye or concluding, which can feel unnatural and awkward.
insights.next_step: Analyze the model execution pipeline for turn 5 to determine why concluding the conversation causes this latency spike.

insights.title: Untrustworthy Metrics at Step c40 Due to Degraded Test Harness
insights.finding: The step representing 40 concurrent calls was executed under degraded harness conditions, recording a worst harness drift of 147.3 ms.
insights.why_it_matters: We cannot draw reliable conclusions from step c40 because the measurements are impacted by the test machine's own capacity limitations rather than the agent's performance.
insights.next_step: Re-run the high-concurrency steps with upgraded test infrastructure to prevent harness degradation.

insights.title: Think-Speak Process is the Main Latency Bottleneck
insights.finding: At 20 concurrent calls, the think-speak p95 latency is 2893.8 ms, which vastly exceeds the endpointing p95 of 375.4 ms and the network round trip p95 of 90.0 ms.
insights.why_it_matters: The delay is almost entirely caused by the agent's thinking and speech response synthesis rather than network round-trip time or silence detection.
insights.next_step: Investigate using smaller, faster LLMs or streaming audio chunks earlier to reduce the think-speak latency.

insights.title: Highly Accurate Task Completion and Transcription Under Load
insights.finding: The judge passed 100.0% of the 20 evaluated calls, and the mean word error rate only shifted slightly from 3.0% at baseline to 3.6% at 20 concurrent calls.
insights.why_it_matters: While load degrades response times, it does not impact the agent's accuracy, compliance with criteria, or transcription quality.
insights.next_step: Maintain the existing Deepgram-based transcription pipeline and model prompting rules.
